facts.text: Dotyville was situated within Indian Territory before Oklahoma officially joined the Union as a state in November 1907.
The Neosho River borders Dotyville to the northeast, influencing the local geography and providing a natural boundary.
Dotyville sits at an elevation of 774 feet, which is characteristic of the gently rolling terrain in the Neosho River valley.
Dotyville experiences a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild winters featuring occasional cold snaps.
Common wildlife in the Dotyville area includes white-tailed deer, wild turkeys, and various bird species adapted to woodland habitats.
Detailed records regarding the precise founding and the origin of the name Dotyville remain limited due to its unincorporated status.
